name: Canastone
description: Canastone (meaning 'Large Canasta') is a three-deck version of Canasta played in Italy, also known as Italian Canasta. Uses 162 cards (three 52-card packs + 6 jokers). Features unique drawing rules (draw 2 from stock OR take discard pile + 1 from stock), variable discard pile size, and special bonuses for wild card and Ace canastas.

content.text: Canastone (meaning 'Large Canasta') is a three-deck version of Canasta played in Italy, also known as Italian Canasta. Uses 162 cards (three 52-card packs + 6 jokers). Features unique drawing rules (draw 2 from stock OR take discard pile + 1 from stock), variable discard pile size, and special bonuses for wild card and Ace canastas.

Canastone is an Italian variant of Canasta that uses three decks instead of two. The name means 'Large Canasta' referring to the larger deck and the potential for more cards in play. It represents the Italian adaptation of the South American game.
4 players in fixed partnerships (partners opposite); can be played with 6 (two teams of 3)

162 cards: three standard 52-card packs plus six jokers. Only colors (red/black) matter, not specific suits. Wild cards: jokers (mattoni) and 2s (pinelle). Natural cards: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4. Threes have special functions.
162-card deck (or special Canastone cards with red/black discs), score sheet

Partnerships by drawing cards (highest vs lowest). Dealer gives 15 cards each. Next card turned up starts discard pile (pozzo). If 3 or wild, keep turning until natural found. If first 3 all wild/3s, redeal. Dealer adds face-down packet to discard pile: size = rank of face-up card (Ace=14, King=13, ..., Four=4). If face-up 2 or joker, pile is frozen (turned sideways). Stock pile (tallone) is remaining cards.
